# Audio AI

The client half of Field Audio: a separate HTTP/WebSocket service that runs generative and analysis models over audio, and the typed vocabulary a box talks to it in. Nothing here loads a model or does inference in the JVM — a box builds a `ModelOperation`, submits it through `FieldAudioClient`, and gets back a job it can poll or watch; the results are immutable server-side *assets* referenced by id, which is why the protocol types carry representation ids rather than samples. Every call is asynchronous and completes off Field's runloop and off the audio callback, so nothing here may be `.get()`-ed from a box's frame. The rest of the category is what you do with a result inside a box: the candidate browser, the EnCodec reconstruction microscope, the beat/pitch analysis viewer and the job monitor, each of them one function returning a self-contained HTML fragment for `display(…)`. Start from `Protocol.kt` for the vocabulary and `FieldAudioClient.kt` for the verbs; [Field Audio service reference](../field_audio_service_reference.md) is the service-side contract the types mirror.

## AnalysisOperations.kt { #analysisoperations-kt }

The three analysis operations, as typed constructors: beats and tempo, monophonic pitch, and
polyphonic transcription.

Each one is a [`ModelOperation`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-modeloperation) factory and nothing more — it validates its arguments here in the
JVM, names the backend that serves it, and packs the parameters into the snake_case keys that
backend expects. Submitting it, waiting for it and drawing it are `FieldAudioClient`'s job.

All three ask for a single candidate, because an analysis of a fixed window with fixed parameters
has one answer; the seed family in `styleCandidates` has no counterpart here. All three also
produce an `.npz` of full-resolution arrays plus, for a drawing, a downsampled
[`AnalysisPreview`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-analysispreview) — see `analysisVisualizationHtml`.

Which to reach for: `multiScaleBeatAnalysis` when you want *when*, and at several time scales at
once, because a tempo estimate is only meaningful relative to a window length;
`monophonicPitchAnalysis` when you know there is one voice and want a continuous F0 with a voiced
probability; `polyphonicPitchAnalysis` when there are chords and you want discrete note events
(and MIDI) rather than a curve.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/noir/audioai/AnalysisOperations.kt`

**Used in:** [Beat and pitch analysis: from source to synchronized views](../audio_ai_analysis.md), [Visualizers, Displays, and Little Instruments](../visualizers.md)

## AudioAssetVisualization.kt { #audioassetvisualization-kt }

The one-line bridge from a Field Audio [`AssetRepresentation`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-assetrepresentation) to Field's general-purpose waveform
player.

It exists so that playing a service asset needs no URL arithmetic: the extension resolves the
binary path and the server-side waveform endpoint against the same-origin `/field-audio` prefix
and hands both to `AudioVisualizer`, which then fetches only the envelope of whatever window the
user is looking at.

## CodecVisualization.kt { #codecvisualization-kt }

The EnCodec reconstruction microscope: what a neural codec kept, what it threw away, and what it
wrote down in between.

A codec round trip is three things that have to be looked at together — the audio in, the discrete
tokens, the audio out — and this file is the rendering half of that view. It is deliberately
browser-free below the top layer: the spectrograms, the waveform and the token map are drawn into
PNG bytes on the JVM, so the same code produces a live box output, a test assertion and the
committed picture on [the EnCodec microscope page](../audio_ai_codec.md).

Everything here needs the bytes locally, which is what `FieldAudioClient.codecVisualizationHtml`
is for — it downloads the three representations off Field's runloop and then renders.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/noir/audioai/CodecVisualization.kt`

## FieldAudioClient.kt { #fieldaudioclient-kt }

The verbs of Field Audio: one client object whose every method is a request to the model
service, plus the typed constructors for the two operations that ship with real controls.

The protocol types — [`AssetRegion`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-assetregion), [`ModelOperation`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-modeloperation), [`JobRecord`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-jobrecord) and the rest — are the
vocabulary; this is what you can *do* with it. The shape to hold on to is that nothing here
blocks and nothing here runs a model in the JVM: a call returns
a `CompletableFuture` that completes on the client's own executor, and the model work happens in
a Python worker that may take minutes. Composing futures (`thenCompose`, `thenAccept`) is
therefore the only correct way to use this from a box — a `.get()` on Field's runloop freezes
the editor for as long as the model takes.

Argument validation happens here, in the JVM, before anything is sent: `require` failures name
the constraint. Everything the service rejects instead arrives as a [`FieldAudioException`](audio-ai.md#fieldaudioclient-kt-fieldaudioexception)
carrying the service's own [`StructuredError`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-structurederror), and a job that fails after being accepted arrives
as a [`FieldAudioJobException`](audio-ai.md#fieldaudioclient-kt-fieldaudiojobexception) from one of the `await…` helpers.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/noir/audioai/FieldAudioClient.kt`

## FieldPersistence.kt { #fieldpersistence-kt }

How a Field document remembers audio work: ids and judgements in a box property, and not one
sample of audio.

The rule this file enforces is that Python is a worker and Field is the authority. The service
owns immutable, content-addressed assets; the document owns which of them it refers to and what
you thought of them. That is why saved state is a [`FieldAudioProjectState`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-fieldaudioprojectstate) of ids rather than
audio, and why reopening a document and re-fetching those ids gets the same bytes back.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/noir/audioai/FieldPersistence.kt`

## JobMonitor.kt { #jobmonitor-kt }

The job monitor: the service's own live view of every durable job, embedded in a box output.

It is an `<iframe>` rather than a Kotlin-rendered table on purpose — the page is served by the
same service that owns the jobs, so it cannot disagree with them, and it needs no polling code on
the Field side. Same-origin through the `/field-audio` prefix, so nothing here reaches across
origins.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/noir/audioai/JobMonitor.kt`

## NpyIntTensor.kt { #npyinttensor-kt }

A dependency-free reader for the integer NPY tensors the audio service emits — the codec token
grids, in practice.

`numpy.kt` already reads `.npy` and `.npz` generally; this is the narrow, self-checking version
for the one shape that matters here (codebooks × frames of small integers), so the codec views
can index tokens by codebook and frame without a general tensor type in between. It refuses what
it cannot represent honestly rather than guessing: Fortran order, an unsupported dtype and a
multi-item batch are all errors with a message.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/noir/audioai/NpyIntTensor.kt`

## Protocol.kt { #protocol-kt }

The wire vocabulary of Field Audio — one Kotlin type per JSON object in the pinned service
contract, and nothing else.

Field Audio runs models out of process: a long-lived Python service owns inference, and a box
talks to it over HTTP and one WebSocket through [`FieldAudioClient`](audio-ai.md#fieldaudioclient-kt-fieldaudioclient). These are the values that
cross that boundary. Every `SerialName` here is the snake_case name the service uses, and the
committed, model-free snapshot of the same contract is published as
[the Field Audio service reference](../field_audio_service_reference.md) — if the two disagree,
the service is right and this file is stale.

### Three facts that explain the shapes

- **Results are assets, not samples.** Everything the service produces is written once, named by
  the SHA-256 of its bytes (`sha256:` followed by 64 hex digits) and referred to afterwards by
  id. That is why a result type carries an [`AssetRepresentation`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-assetrepresentation) rather than a `FloatArray`: the
  audio is still on the service, and `FieldAudioClient.download` is how bytes reach the JVM.
- **Work is a job, not a call.** Submitting an operation returns a [`JobAccepted`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-jobaccepted) immediately;
  the outcome arrives later as a [`JobRecord`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-jobrecord) you poll or a stream of [`ProgressEvent`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-progressevent)s you watch.
- **Identical requests are not repeated.** The service hashes the request (ignoring
  `ModelOperation.forceRegenerate`) into `JobRecord.requestHash` and returns the stored result
  when it has seen that hash before, with `cacheHit = true` and a job that is already complete.

### Times, ids and timestamps

All times and durations are **seconds** as `Double` unless the property name says otherwise.
`createdAt`, `updatedAt` and `ProgressEvent.at` are ISO-8601 UTC timestamp *strings*, kept as
text because nothing in Field parses them and a string round-trips through project persistence
unchanged. Ids are opaque and prefixed by kind: `sha256:` for assets, `rep_` for
representations, `job_`, `op_`, `cset_`, `codec_` and `analysis_` for the rest.

The client decodes with `ignoreUnknownKeys`, so a newer service that adds a field will not break
an older Field; the reverse is not true, because the service rejects unknown fields it is sent.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/noir/audioai/Protocol.kt`

### AssetRegion { #protocol-kt-assetregion }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">AssetRegion</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">@</span><span class="nc">SerialName</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">&quot;asset&#95;id&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">assetId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="p">@</span><span class="nc">SerialName</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">&quot;start&#95;seconds&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">startSeconds</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="p">@</span><span class="nc">SerialName</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">&quot;duration&#95;seconds&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">durationSeconds</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

A time window inside one asset — the unit of "what should the model listen to".

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">assetId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Content address of the asset to read, of the form `sha256:` plus 64 hex digits. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">startSeconds</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | Offset of the window from the start of the asset, in seconds; must be non-negative. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">durationSeconds</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | Length of the window in seconds; must be strictly positive. |

One concrete encoding of one asset's bytes: what format they are in, and where to fetch them.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">id</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Stable representation id: `rep_` followed by a digest of the asset, role and format. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">assetId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Content address of the asset these bytes belong to. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">role</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | What this representation is *for*, as one of the role names described above. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">mediaType</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | IANA media type of the bytes, e.g. `audio/wav` or `application/x-npy`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">sampleRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Sample rate of these bytes in Hz, or null when the representation is not audio. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">channels</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Channel count of these bytes, or null when the representation is not audio. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">frameCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Length in sample frames, or null when the representation is not audio. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">durationSeconds</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Length in seconds, or null when the representation is not audio. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">nativeSampleRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | The rate the producing model actually worked at, when `sampleRate` is a resample of it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">resamplingMethod</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | How the resample to `sampleRate` was done, when one happened; null when nothing was resampled. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">binaryUrl</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Service-relative path to the bytes: `/v1/representations/{id}/content`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">metadata</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">JsonObject</span></code> | Free-form provenance the producing step attached — backend id and revision, operation and request hash, seed, source asset, decoded WAV header. Nothing in Field interprets it. |

### AudioAsset { #protocol-kt-audioasset }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">AudioAsset</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">id</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="p">@</span><span class="nc">SerialName</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">&quot;byte&#95;size&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">byteSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="p">@</span><span class="nc">SerialName</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">&quot;created&#95;at&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">createdAt</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">representations</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">AssetRepresentation</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">metadata</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">JsonObject</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">JsonObject</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nf">emptyMap</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

An immutable blob of audio on the service, plus every representation of it.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">id</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Content address of the bytes: `sha256:` followed by 64 hex digits. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">byteSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code> | Size of the underlying bytes, in bytes. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">createdAt</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the first time these bytes were stored. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">representations</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">AssetRepresentation</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | Every materialised view of this asset, oldest first. See `AssetRepresentation.role`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">metadata</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">JsonObject</span></code> | Free-form provenance recorded at import or generation time; not interpreted by Field. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">durationSeconds</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Duration of the first representation that declares one, in seconds, or null if none does. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">sampleRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Sample rate of the first representation that declares one, with the caveat on `durationSeconds`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">channels</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Channel count of the first representation that declares one, with the caveat on `durationSeconds`. |

A min/max envelope of one representation over one time window — what a waveform display draws.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">representationId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The representation that was summarised. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">startSeconds</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | Start of the summarised window, in seconds from the start of the representation. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">durationSeconds</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | Length of the summarised window, in seconds. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">sampleRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Sample rate of the underlying audio in Hz — the envelope itself is not sampled at this rate. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">channels</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Number of channels, and so the outer length of `minimum` and `maximum`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">pointCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Points per channel. Never more than the window's frame count, so a short window returns fewer. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">minimum</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | Per-channel minima, indexed ``channel``, nominally in −1..1. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">maximum</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | Per-channel maxima, indexed ``channel``, nominally in −1..1. |

### JobState { #protocol-kt-jobstate }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">enum</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">JobState</span></code>

Where a job has got to. Most of these are progress narration; four of them are the end.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">terminal</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | True once the job will not change again: `COMPLETE`, `CANCELLED`, `COMPLETED_BEFORE_CANCELLATION` or `FAILED`. |

### JobAccepted { #protocol-kt-jobaccepted }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">JobAccepted</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">@</span><span class="nc">SerialName</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">&quot;job&#95;id&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">jobId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">state</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">JobState</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="p">@</span><span class="nc">SerialName</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">&quot;request&#95;hash&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">requestHash</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="p">@</span><span class="nc">SerialName</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">&quot;resolved&#95;backend&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">resolvedBackend</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="p">@</span><span class="nc">SerialName</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">&quot;cache&#95;hit&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">cacheHit</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

The immediate answer to submitting a [`ModelOperation`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-modeloperation): a job exists, and here is how to follow it.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">jobId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Id of the job to poll (`FieldAudioClient.inspect`) or watch (`watch`): `job_` plus a UUID. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">state</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">JobState</span></code> | State at acceptance: `QUEUED` for real work, `COMPLETE` when `cacheHit` is true. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">requestHash</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Hash of the submitted request; identical requests share it, which is how caching happens. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">resolvedBackend</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The backend the service actually chose, whether or not one was preferred. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">cacheHit</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | True when this request had been served before and no model was run. |

### StructuredError { #protocol-kt-structurederror }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">StructuredError</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">code</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">message</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">retryable</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">details</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">JsonObject</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">JsonObject</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nf">emptyMap</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

A failure the service could name, as opposed to an HTTP status.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">code</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | A code from the service's fixed vocabulary — `ASSET_NOT_FOUND`, `INVALID_TIME_RANGE`, `UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION`, `MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE`, `MODEL_LOAD_FAILED`, `MODEL_OUT_OF_MEMORY`, `GENERATION_FAILED`, `ENCODING_FAILED`, `DECODING_FAILED`, `ANALYSIS_FAILED`, `RESAMPLING_FAILED`, `JOB_CANCELLED`, `WORKER_UNAVAILABLE`, `PROTOCOL_VERSION_MISMATCH`, `CACHE_CORRUPTION`. Typed as a `String` so an unrecognised future code still decodes. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">message</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Human-readable detail. Used as-is in the exception message; not machine-parseable. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">retryable</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | The service's own hint that retrying unchanged might work. A job that fails mid-run sets it false. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">details</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">JsonObject</span></code> | Extra machine-readable context, e.g. the worker exception type. |

The durable state of one job — the thing polling returns.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">id</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The job id: `job_` plus a UUID. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">operationId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The stored operation this job ran, `op_` plus a UUID. Several jobs share one on a cache hit. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">requestHash</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Hash of the request; the cache key. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">state</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">JobState</span></code> | Where the job has got to. Check `JobState.terminal` before reading a result id. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">resolvedBackend</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The backend that ran, or is running, this job. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">progress</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | Fraction of the job done, 0..1. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">createdAt</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of when the job was accepted. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">updatedAt</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the last state or progress change. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">error</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">StructuredError</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Why the job failed, when it did. Null in every other state. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">candidateSetId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Set when a `generate.*` job completed: fetch it with `FieldAudioClient.candidateSet`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">codecResultId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Set when a `codec.*` job completed: fetch it with `FieldAudioClient.codecResult`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">analysisResultId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Set when an `analysis.*` job completed: fetch it with `FieldAudioClient.analysisResult`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">cacheHit</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | True when this job was answered from the result cache without running a model. |

A [`JobRecord`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-jobrecord) as it appears in the job *list*, with the two fields that make a list readable: what was asked for, and by whom.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">id</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The job id: `job_` plus a UUID. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">operationId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The stored operation this job ran. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">requestHash</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Hash of the request; the cache key. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">state</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">JobState</span></code> | Where the job has got to. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">resolvedBackend</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The backend that ran, or is running, this job. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">progress</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | Fraction of the job done, 0..1; see `JobRecord.progress`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">createdAt</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of when the job was accepted. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">updatedAt</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the last state or progress change. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">error</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">StructuredError</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Why the job failed, when it did. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">candidateSetId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Set when a `generate.*` job completed. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">codecResultId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Set when a `codec.*` job completed. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">analysisResultId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Set when an `analysis.*` job completed. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">cacheHit</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | True when this job was answered from the result cache. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">operation</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The dotted operation name that was requested — the column a job list is really scanned by. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">requestedBy</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Whatever `ModelOperation.requestedBy` was set to, or null. |

One alternative in a generated family, with its provenance and your verdict on it.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">asset</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AudioAsset</span></code> | The model-native output asset, described in full so no second request is needed. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">operationId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The stored operation that produced the whole family. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">index</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Position in the family, from zero. The candidate board displays it one-based. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">seed</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code> | The RNG seed this alternative was generated with — resubmit it to get this take back. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">nativeRepresentationId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Representation id of the model's own output, at the model's own sample rate. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">proxyRepresentationId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Representation id of the 48 kHz WAV to audition. This is the one to play. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">splicePreviewRepresentationId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Representation id of the source crossfaded into this candidate, when the backend made one. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">nativeRepresentation</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AssetRepresentation</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Inline metadata for `nativeRepresentationId`, when the service inlined it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">proxyRepresentation</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AssetRepresentation</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Inline metadata for `proxyRepresentationId`, when the service inlined it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">splicePreviewRepresentation</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AssetRepresentation</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Inline metadata for `splicePreviewRepresentationId`, when there is one. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">score</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | A backend-computed score, if that backend computes one. Not comparable across backends. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">gestureEvaluation</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">GestureEvaluation</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | How the gesture board scored this candidate, when one produced it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">rating</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Your rating, as last written back with `FieldAudioClient.judge`. The board's slider spans −1..1. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">selected</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | Your selection flag, as last written back. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="k">annotation</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Your note, as last written back. |

### CandidateSet { #protocol-kt-candidateset }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">CandidateSet</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">id</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="p">@</span><span class="nc">SerialName</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">&quot;operation&#95;id&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">operationId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="p">@</span><span class="nc">SerialName</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">&quot;request&#95;hash&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">requestHash</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">candidates</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Candidate</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="p">@</span><span class="nc">SerialName</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">&quot;created&#95;at&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">createdAt</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

The whole family a `generate.*` job produced, in one immutable, re-fetchable value.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">id</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Id of the set: `cset_` plus a UUID. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">operationId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The stored operation that produced it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">requestHash</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Hash of the request; two identical requests resolve to the same stored set. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">candidates</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Candidate</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | The alternatives, in `Candidate.index` order. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">createdAt</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of when the set was written. |

### ReconstructionMetrics { #protocol-kt-reconstructionmetrics }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ReconstructionMetrics</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">rmse</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="p">@</span><span class="nc">SerialName</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">&quot;snr&#95;db&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">snrDb</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="p">@</span><span class="nc">SerialName</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">&quot;spectral&#95;convergence&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">spectralConvergence</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

How far a codec round trip's output is from its input, by three different measures.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">rmse</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | Root-mean-square error in normalised sample units; 0 is a perfect reconstruction. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">snrDb</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Signal-to-noise ratio in dB, when the backend reports one. Higher is better. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">spectralConvergence</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Relative spectral distance, when the backend reports one. Lower is better. |

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">id</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Id of the result: `codec_` plus a UUID. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">operationId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The stored operation that produced it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">requestHash</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Hash of the request. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">source</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AssetRegion</span></code> | The source window that was reconstructed. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">modelInput</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AssetRepresentation</span></code> | The audio the codec actually saw: the window, resampled to the model's rate. Compare against this. |

| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">createdAt</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of when the result was written. |

### AnalysisSeries { #protocol-kt-analysisseries }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">AnalysisSeries</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">label</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">unit</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="p">@</span><span class="nc">SerialName</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">&quot;times&#95;seconds&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">timesSeconds</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">values</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">metadata</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">JsonObject</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">JsonObject</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nf">emptyMap</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

One named curve inside an [`AnalysisPreview`](audio-ai.md#protocol-kt-analysispreview): a time axis, a value axis, and what to call them.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Machine name, e.g. `onset_strength`, `frequency_hz`, `tempo_0_bpm`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">label</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Human label for a legend, e.g. `tempo · 4 s`. Falls back to `name`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">unit</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Unit of `values` where one applies, e.g. `Hz` or `bpm`; null for a dimensionless curve. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">timesSeconds</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | Sample times in seconds from the start of the analysed window; null where non-finite. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">values</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | The curve itself, parallel to `timesSeconds`; null where non-finite. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">metadata</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">JsonObject</span></code> | Per-series extras, e.g. the `scale_seconds` a multi-scale tempo track was measured at. |

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">AnalysisNote</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">@</span><span class="nc">SerialName</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">&quot;start&#95;seconds&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">startSeconds</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="p">@</span><span class="nc">SerialName</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">&quot;end&#95;seconds&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">endSeconds</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">midi</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">amplitude</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

| --- | --- |

| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">jobId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The job this event belongs to. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">state</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">JobState</span></code> | The state the job entered. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">progress</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | Fraction done, 0..1; see `JobRecord.progress`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">message</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | A short human-readable note, e.g. "making 48 kHz audition proxy". Null when there is nothing to say. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">candidateIndex</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Which candidate this event is about, for a family generated one at a time. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">at</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the event. |
